body.content: Fixture cost: The lease-mismatch test can be covered by a minimal fixture that freezes a single lease binding and mutates its drift field, avoiding the need for a full manifest. The seat-binding test may require a slightly more complex fixture to represent the school-to-seat relationship, but it should still avoid rebuilding the entire routing topology.
body.why_keep_this: This note assesses the fixture cost, ensuring the suite adheres to the requirement of avoiding a full manifest where a frozen lease suffices.

body.content: Attack surface: The firewall's attack surface includes the route lease validation logic and the school-to-seat binding logic. For the lease-mismatch, the attack surface is the synchronous precondition check before any provider call. For the seat-binding, it is the endpoint identity comparison. Mutations that bypass these checks represent the primary false-green risk.
body.why_keep_this: This note maps the attack surface for both refusals, providing a foundation for the forbidden cases in the regression suite.

body.content: False-green risk: For the lease-mismatch, a mutation that performs a homogeneous identity comparison ignoring drift fields would pass silently. For the seat-binding, a mutation that homogenizes the identity check between the school and seat would also pass silently. The forbidden cases must explicitly target these mutations.
body.why_keep_this: This note identifies the specific false-green risks for each test, guiding the design of the program: and rubric: eval forms.

body.relation_hint: The attack surface analysis informs the fixture cost assessment by identifying the minimal components needed for testing.
The attack surface analysis directly identifies the false-green risks that the forbidden cases must address.
The fixture cost assessment constraints the design of the false-green risk tests by limiting the complexity of the test setup.
